Title: BCCK named official venue for national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Sarawak has been officially named the venue for the national-level Malaysia Day celebrations on Sept 16.
The decision to hold the main celebration indoors was made to provide a climate-controlled and safe environment for dignitaries and cultural troupes, in view of the current haze affecting parts of Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.
Information Department (JAPEN) Cyber Media Division assistant director Yumna Baharuddin said Sarawak's selection as host aligns with the 2020 Cabinet decision to implement a rotational system between Sarawak, Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.
"This rotational system ensures that every Malaysian, regardless of geographic location, shares directly in the spirit and historical resonance of Malaysia Day.
"Following Penang's hosting in 2025, bringing the celebrations back to Sarawak underscores the Federal Government's unwavering commitment to strengthening national integration across all regions," she said today.
Elaborating on the significance of the date, Yumna emphasised the distinct historical significance of the two national observances.
"While Aug 31 commemorates the independence of the Federation of Malaya in 1957, Sept 16 marks the 1963 historic unification of Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore into a single sovereign federation," she said.
This year's celebration retains the theme "Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati" (Prosperity Enjoyed Together), paired with Sarawak's unity tagline "Segulai Sejalai" (Walking Hand-in-Hand).
The main ceremonial event at BCCK will feature an array of symbolic and cultural performances, including an inter-ethnic welcoming segment blending silat,
hadra, gendang pampat
and lion dance performances.
It will also include the signing of the Malaysia Proclamation Book by national and state leaders.
The historical volume was transported under the custody of the Sabah State Archives, pursuant to the Sabah State Records and Archives Enactment 2007.
Other highlights include the ceremonial cutting of
pulut kuning
and a tri-state artiste showcase featuring prominent performers Dayang Nurfaizah, Aizat Amdan and Stacy.
Japen and its partner agencies have also arranged a series of satellite events from Sept 10 to 16.
These include the Formation Corridor Exhibition at Plaza Merdeka, division-level pop-up exhibitions across 10 Sarawak divisions, as well as activities in Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur to ensure widespread public participation. — BERNAMA

Title: Great Eastern targets affluent customers with new offerings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Great Eastern Life Assurance (Malaysia) Bhd has launched Great Prestige, a dedicated proposition for affluent customers, alongside the unveiling of the Great Prestige Suite at Prince Court Medical Centre, Malaysia's first dedicated premium insurance suite within a medical centre.
Great Prestige is designed to support affluent customers as their financial priorities evolve over time while the Great Prestige Suite brings together key elements of the insurance onboarding process in one dedicated environment.
Great Eastern said customers can complete the required medical assessments seamlessly and receive on-site underwriting support guided by a dedicated prestige ambassador who coordinates the journey.
"As our customers progress through various stages of life, their priorities naturally change. The conversation moves beyond building wealth to preserving what they have accumulated, through relevant insurance solutions, specialist advisory, and a personalised level of service.
"Great Prestige brings these priorities together through relevant insurance solutions, specialist advisory, and a personalised level of service. It is about recognising what our customers value, including their time, and making their experience more seamless, personal, and convenient," said Great Eastern chief executive officer Datuk Koh Yaw Hui.
Under solutions, Great Prestige offers insurance solutions across wealth creation, wealth preservation and legacy planning that caters to both onshore and offshore needs. These include Prestige Heritage Global, Prestige Heritage Index and Prestige Wealth Index.
Through advisory, customers can access specialist expertise beyond insurance in areas such as tax and business advisory, legal advisory, estate planning and investment advisory, providing guidance where additional expertise may be required.
Beyond the suite, customers can enjoy selected healthcare privileges, legacy and wealth talks and curated lifestyle experiences designed around their evolving needs and interests.

Title: After child mauled, Johor orders operation to capture five stray dogs
Article:
Pix: Najmi Nor'Azam
JOHOR BARU: Johor has ordered a major operation to track down and capture five stray dogs that mauled a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat.
State Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said the dogs must be captured and tested for rabies, with the operation to be intensified for at least a week. The incident happened last Saturday.
He said ruling out rabies was crucial not only for the safety of residents but also to ease concerns over Nur Haira Wafiqah Muhammad Hamizi's long-term recovery.
"The hospital is also concerned about whether the dogs that attacked the child were carrying rabies.
"Immediate action is therefore needed to capture and examine the dogs. If they are confirmed to be rabies-free, it will give some relief to the doctors and her parents, as this concern could affect the child's recovery," he said.
Fared said the operation involved the Batu Pahat district office, Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police.
"We will not rely on a single method. Surveillance, monitoring and intelligence-gathering will be intensified.
"Our commitment is to resolve the stray dog problem in the area and prevent a similar incident from happening to others," he said.
He said the Batu Pahat Municipal Council and DVS had previously conducted operations on Aug 12, 26 and 30, resulting in 22 stray dogs being captured in the area.
However, the continued presence of stray dogs showed that capture efforts needed to be stepped up, he said.
Fared said the state government would fully cover Nur Haira's medical treatment and rehabilitation costs, with the toddler expected to undergo a lengthy recovery.
He also urged the hospital to pay close attention to the family's emotional wellbeing, particularly Nur Haira's 12-year-old brother, who remains traumatised after witnessing the attack.
Fared said this after visiting Nur Haira, who is being treated at Sultanah Aminah Hospital's paediatric intensive care unit, here today.

Title: PISA 2025: Malaysia improves in Science, Reading but slips in Mathematics
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia recorded encouraging improvements in the Science and Reading literacy domains under the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2025.
Results from the triennial PISA study showed Science literacy rose three points to 419, while Reading literacy increased five points to 393 compared with the PISA 2022 report.
However, the average score for Mathematics literacy declined by 11 points to 397 compared with the performance recorded three years ago.

Title: Nepalis mark a year since deadly protests that toppled government
Article:
KATHMANDU: Dozens of young people congregated at Nepal's burnt-out parliament building on Tuesday to mark the anniversary of deadly anti-corruption protests that toppled the former government.
The gathering in memory of those who died in the demonstrations came as the Himalayan nation continues to mourn the vast loss of life from devastating floods two weeks ago.
The rallies on September 8-9, 2025, were initially sparked by anger over a brief government ban on social media but were driven by deeper frustration over economic hardship, corruption and entrenched political practices.
The unrest caused the deaths of 76 people and the torching of the parliament building in the capital Kathmandu, as well as the prime minister's office and other government buildings.
It also led to the downfall of the administration of KP Sharma Oli, setting in motion a series of events that culminated with the election of youthful Prime Minister Balendra Shah in March.
"The loss of life was of course terrible. But the impact on politics was worth it, we have seen changes," said former protester Aastha Shrestha, 23, on the grounds of the ruined building.
"It feels like the (current) government values the sacrifice we made," she told AFP next to a stack of burnt vehicles.
Banners bearing photos of people killed in the protests were hung in the parliament grounds.
Shah said on X that he hoped the anniversary would "inspire us all to move forward towards building a fair, transparent, and opportunity-filled Nepal."
Sushila Karki, who led Nepal as interim prime minister after Oli's government was overthrown, paid tribute to "all the brave individuals who lost their lives."
"Let us all perform our duties honestly, responsibly, and vigilantly... so that a situation never arises again in which people are forced to take to the streets once more for good governance and change," she said in a social media post.
An inquiry commission set up to investigate the violence submitted its report in April and recommended further probes against several officials including Oli.
The majority of the victims – 51 people – were shot dead, many in the head or chest, according to the report.
But there has been little genuine accountability, said Anish Acharya, 19, who came with flowers to pay his respects.
"Why did we sacrifice our lives, what did we get? There is no hope that change will come. Oli was arrested the next day but what then? The culprits are out and walking free," he told AFP.
"The government has not valued our sacrifices and demands."
Shah's administration is facing its toughest challenge since taking power as it leads rescue and recovery efforts following cataclysmic glacial floods on the border with China.
The Aug 26 disaster killed at least 1,399 people in the two countries, including 1,356 in Nepal, according to official tolls.
A total of 5,500 people are still missing in Nepal and China.

Title: Dismembered body case: Senior citizen's murder charge transferred to High Court
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The magistrate's court today ordered the case of a senior citizen charged with murdering a woman whose dismembered body was found to be transferred to the High Court.
Magistrate Dzul Elmy Yunus made the order after allowing the prosecution's application to transfer the case involving Piluta Samad, 72.
The prosecution informed the court that it had received instructions to transfer the case to the High Court here.
Piluta is charged with murdering
Hamidah Husin @ Lisa, 44, between 6pm and 7pm on Feb 11, 2026, at an unnumbered house in Kampung Sri Kenangan, Jalan Sepanggar.
The charge is framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment for between 30 and 40 years. If the death penalty is not imposed, a male offender below the age of 50 is also liable to a minimum of 12 strokes of the rotan.
No plea was recorded when Piluta was brought before the magistrate's court on Feb 27, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The court on April 15 ordered Piluta to undergo 30 days of observation at Hospital Mesra following an application by his legal team for him to undergo a mental assessment under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
On May 15, the court granted a one-month extension for Piluta's psychiatric assessment.
On July 23, a hospital report found Piluta fit to stand trial and not suffering from any mental illness.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Ronnie Anthony appeared for the prosecution, while Piluta was represented by lawyers Datuk Ram Singh, Joan Goh, Ian Vun and Prem Elmer Ganasan.

Title: 5.2-magnitude earthquake hits Indonesia's Flores region
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale occurred in the Flores region of Indonesia at 12.40pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said in a statement that the earthquake was detected at coordinates 8.1 degrees South and 120.8 degrees East, about 240 kilometres (km) east of Bima, Indonesia.
The earthquake occurred at a depth of 34km.
"It posed no tsunami threat to Malaysia," added MetMalaysia.

Title: Thieves steal three paintings from Renoir Museum on French Riviera
Article:
PARIS: Thieves stole three paintings from the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera early on Tuesday, the local mayor said.
The raiders broke into the museum a little before 6am and took four paintings, Cagnes-sur-Mer mayor Bryan Masson said on his Facebook page.
Police spotted the thieves and gave chase, during which they dropped one painting but escaped with the other three, he said.
"Attacking the Renoir museum is attacking a part of the history and heritage of Cagnes-sur-Mer. These actions are particularly serious," Masson said in his message.
The museum was created in 1960 in the mansion of the impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir on a hill in Cagnes-sur-Mer, near Nice, where he died in 1919.
The collection on display in the museum includes 13 paintings from the master and some 40 sculptures, furniture and photographs.
Masson did not identify the paintings that were stolen. Renoir's most valuable works have fetched dozens of millions of dollars at auctions in the past.
Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad hoc ​opportunists recruited through social media, pan-European police body Europol said last month.
The heist at ‌the Louvre Museum in Paris in October last year was a prime example of this, Europol said, as the thieves threatened guards and visitors and stole €88 million (US$102.3 million) worth of jewels, such ​as Empress Eugenie's tiara.

Title: Family reported missing took children hiking to limit phone use
Article:
GERIK: Taking up mountain hiking has been a way for Trans Gerah (Trans GBB) expedition hiker Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin to keep his two children away from excessive mobile phone use.
The 39-year-old civil engineer said he turned to hiking after trying various activities, including badminton and swimming, to prevent his children, Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, nine, from becoming overly dependent on gadgets.
"The problem was that they had started becoming addicted to mobile phones, so I looked for ways to prevent them from spending too much time on their phones.
"I tried all sorts of things, including badminton and swimming, but those activities only lasted one or two hours. So, I tried hiking," he said.
Wan Ahmad Aslam said their hiking initially involved only half-day activities before the family progressed to longer expeditions lasting four, five and six days, with their previous longest expedition lasting eight days.
"This is the longest one so far," he said when met at the Gerik District Police Headquarters here today.
He said his children had been actively hiking for the past two years, although he had taken them along on outdoor trips since they were young.
"I have taken them along since they were in a stroller, but they only became really active about two years ago.
"As far as I can remember, this is our eighth Trans expedition as a family. Based on my experience, children are physically more resilient than adults.
"We just need to manage their mental state, make sure they are happy and enjoy the journey," he said.
On the expedition, Wan Ahmad Aslam said the group had not actually got lost but had taken longer than expected due to several obstacles along the route.
"Actually, we were in control while in the jungle. We knew where we were, how much food we had and that none of us was injured.
"We were not lost. We were just worried that our families would lodge a police report, which eventually happened," he said.
He said the group had progressed at a slower pace than expected, covering only about two to three kilometres a day compared with their initial target of between eight and 10 kilometres.
This led them to discuss whether to turn back or continue before deciding to look for a water source and cut across the original trail.
Wan Ahmad Aslam said their food supplies were still sufficient until the 10th day despite the expedition exceeding its original schedule.
"I can say that we still had food until the 10th day. The mountain guides, knowing that I was bringing my children, also brought additional supplies for our family.
"On the final day, I still had Power Gel, Hydro Gel and ORS, while we still had rice," he said.
Earlier, Wan Ahmad Aslam, his family and two mountain guides leading the group were
found safe
at Kem Kulim and brought down this morning via the Trojan Temengor base before being handed over to their respective family members.

Title: Balai Seni Negara, Media Prima explore creative collaboration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Media Prima Bhd today hosted a 14-member delegation from the National Art Gallery at Balai Berita to explore strategic creative collaborations and strengthen communication between the two organisations.
Led by the National Art Galley deputy director-general (operations) Rohana Mohd Yusof, the delegation met Media Prima's editorial leadership to discuss ways to connect national art initiatives with wider public audiences.
Rohana said stronger media partnerships could help showcase the country's rich art collections while encouraging greater appreciation of local culture.
"We hope that Balai Seni Negara and Media Prima Bhd can collaborate on future initiatives," she said.
Media Prima was represented by Television Networks News and Current Affairs group editor Datuk Azhari Muhidin and Media Prima Omnia Government Unit general manager Shanaz Md Azli.
The gallery's representatives also toured Media Prima's broadcast studios, REV Media Group and the newsrooms of The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd.

Title: Presence of Serbian officials at Mladic funeral 'deeply regrettable': EU chiefs
Article:
BRUSSELS: The presence of Serbian officials at the funeral of war criminal Ratko Mladic was "deeply regrettable", EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa said Tuesday.
Serbia's commemoration of the so-called "Butcher of Bosnia" – who was buried Monday in a service attended by thousands – has put Brussels on a collision course with Belgrade, which is a candidate country to join the EU.
"The images from Ratko Mladic's funeral yesterday in Belgrade were shocking," European Commission president Von der Leyen and European Council boss Costa wrote online.
"The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable."
The pair said the move demonstrated "a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe's recent history and contradict the values underpinning Serbia's path towards the European Union."
Mladic died in The Hague last month, aged 84, after being convicted of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the 1990s Bosnian war.
Serbian Justice Minister Nenad Vujic initially announced "military and state honours" for Mladic, triggering international outrage, before President Aleksandar Vucic tempered the decision.
Vucic has rejected accusations of glorifying the former general, describing the service as in keeping with the family's wishes.
The EU has yet to say what the consequences could be for Serbia's efforts to join the 27-nation bloc.
The EU's enlargement chief Marta Kos already scrapped a visit to Belgrade and its looks likely von der Leyen will skip Serbia on an upcoming tour of the Balkans.

Title: Zahid: University autonomy must come with accountability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Greater university autonomy must now be accompanied by measurable accountability for the quality of learning and graduate mobility, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said attention should now turn to legislation that would provide a new legal and governance framework for higher education institutions following the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku).
"As a former student activist, I hope that without Auku, students will be at the forefront of knowledge and professionalism," he said in his closing address at the Malay Education Convention at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
He said the new framework should give universities greater autonomy while maintaining accountability for their performance and outcomes.
Zahid said students should be more involved in decision-making and contribute fresh ideas.
"They do not necessarily need to take to the streets, speak at debate corners every week or hold weekly marches wearing different-coloured shirts.
"I am confident that student leaders and the wider student body will demonstrate greater thinking without Auku restricting their thinking," he said.
Zahid said the new legislation should not be used to restrict students and academics through other means.
"Do not restrict students through other means, and do not restrict academics through other means.
"Through today's convention, we place our trust in Higher Education Minister (Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir) to translate our responsibilities and aspirations into action," he added.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced last month that the government would
abolish Auku
to give students greater freedom to express their views, think independently and participate in politics.S

Title: UiTM student death classified as sudden death pending pathologist report
Article:
MARAN: The death of a Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) student during an endurance competition last week has been classified as a sudden death pending the pathologist's report, police said.
Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21, experienced breathing difficulties during the endurance challenge on Sept 4 before dying at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital in Temerloh the following day.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said preliminary investigations found no signs of foul play.
"As of now, police have opened an investigation paper and classified the case as a sudden death. We will wait for the pathologist's report," he told NST.
Fadhlan Fakhry, who was from UiTM Seremban, Negri Sembilan, was taken to Jengka Hospital along with eight other participants after experiencing breathing difficulties at 9.57pm on Sept 4. He and two others were later transferred to Hoshas after their conditions worsened.
Wong said all 521 participants in the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge had undergone health screenings for the programme at UiTM Jengka before taking part in the activities.
"Only those who passed the checks were allowed to participate," he said.
Meanwhile, Wong said three of the hospitalised students were allowed to return home yesterday, while five others continued to receive medical care.
The endurance programme is an annual physical and mental competition designed to test students' physical strength, tactical skills, agility and teamwork.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor seeks early cloud seeding as Super El Nino looms
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor will seek early cloud-seeding operations ahead of the expected onset of severe drought conditions linked to a Super El Nino from October to December, as the state steps up preparations to safeguard its water reserves.
State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the state government had already engaged the National Disaster Management Agency on preparations for cloud seeding.
"We may seek cloud seeding earlier this time, before the drought sets in.
"However, we have been informed that cloud seeding was carried out in several areas outside Johor due to the haze and other issues," he said.
He said all 17 dams in the state remained under control, although several were being closely monitored for declining water levels.
"Nothing is critical at the moment. Everything is under control. We monitor all 17 dams daily."
Fazli said the state was assessing which dams required closer attention, with Machap and Lok Heng among those considered vulnerable based on previous critical conditions, while Gunung Pulai was currently at the alert level.
"Some dams can last up to a year, while others can last six months. The one we need to watch closely is Gunung Pulai.
"Previously, Machap was the most affected, but this year we expect Gunung Pulai could face greater pressure as we are seeing a downward trend there. We have yet to decide which dams will be prioritised," he said.
Fazli said the state was also considering smaller-scale measures to strengthen water security, including pumping water between sources.
At Lok Heng Dam, a desalination plant had been installed, while additional pumps were being deployed at Machap Dam to increase water discharge into the river supplying its water treatment plant.
He said the measures were part of the state's contingency preparations based on challenges experienced during previous periods of prolonged dry weather.
Fazli was speaking to reporters after attending an engagement programme with taxi drivers in conjunction with Visit Johor 2026 at the Johor Tourism Information Centre today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Explainer: Where the haze is coming from and how it reaches Malaysia
Article:
KUCHING: Fires across Indonesia's Borneo and Sumatra islands have fuelled haze in Malaysia and other parts of Southeast Asia, with smoke drifting across borders.
The fires pushed air quality to hazardous levels, prompting emergency measures and school closures in Sarawak.
Here is what you need to know about where the hotspots were concentrated.
WHERE WERE THE HOTSPOTS?
Most of the fires were concentrated on Borneo, which Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, as well as Sumatra, according to AFP.
Between Aug 28 and Sept 3, fires across the archipelago released more than 23 million metric tonnes of carbon emissions, according to the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) Fire Emissions Watch portal.
[[nid:1528271]]
This was higher than the 20.7 million metric tonnes recorded over the same period in 2015, which was also a strong El Niño year, according to CAMS.
The concentration of fires in Kalimantan was particularly significant for Sarawak, as smoke from fires in Indonesian Borneo drifted across the border, affecting areas in southern Sarawak.
HOW BAD WAS THE IMPACT?
The smoke caused widespread disruption across Indonesia and neighbouring countries, with millions of people exposed to deteriorating air quality.
In Sarawak, the Air Pollutant Index (API) in Serian peaked at 521, exceeding the critical level of 500.
The Education Ministry ordered 647 schools across Sarawak to close from Sept 7 to Sept 11 to protect pupils from exposure to dangerous levels of air pollution.
[[nid:1528270]]
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to a state of emergency being declared in Sarawak's Serian Division, which borders Kalimantan, to safeguard public health and safety.
In Indonesia, more than five million people across Borneo and Sumatra were directly exposed to health risks from the haze, according to Deputy Health Minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono.
More than 1.4 million students were also attending classes remotely as schools were closed in areas affected by worsening air quality.
The United Nations has warned that a very strong El Niño is developing and could intensify in the coming months, raising the risk of extreme weather into 2027.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NCT smart industrial park nears 90pct take-up
Article:
SEPANG: NCT Alliance Bhd has started handing over vacant possession of the first phase of its NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP) in South Selangor, with the 280-unit phase already recording a take-up rate of nearly 90 per cent.
NCT Alliance executive director Yap Chun Theng said the industrial park will house businesses from various sectors, with a strong focus on technology.
"Our focus is high on technology, but we also have several industries such as automotive, hospitality and the environmental, social and governance sector.
"We also have the waste sector, where we can use technology to replace or manage waste from kitchens. So, we have several industries that are included.
"We do not limit the industries that are included," he said at a press conference after the launch of the NSIP's new phase today.
Yap said most of the businesses currently taking up space at the industrial park were local small and medium enterprises (SMEs), although the developer was also in discussions with an international data centre operator.
"Currently, we have a lot of SMEs that are included. Most of them are local. But now we have a discussion with a data centre party, and we have made an announcement to Bursa Malaysia. They will be the international players," he said.
The property developer also launched KM2, the second phase of NSIP, marking the next stage of the industrial park's development and expansion.
The phase will add 241 industrial units to meet growing demand for manufacturing and industrial space in Selangor.
Following the groundbreaking ceremony last year, KM2 will comprise detached, semi-detached, cluster and terrace factories, as well as industrial land parcels, supported by enhanced smart infrastructure.
The development is part of NSIP, which spans about 368.3 hectares and has a gross development value of RM10.2 billion.
The event was officiated by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Also in attendance were Selangor state executive councillor for investment, trade and mobility Ng Sze Han, NCT Alliance executive chairman and group managing director Datuk Seri Yap Ngan Choy and NCT Alliance executive director Datuk Yap Fook Choy.
Amirudin said the park's progress demonstrated the importance of collaboration between the private sector, the state government and relevant agencies in advancing industrial development in the region.
"NSIP has an important role within the Integrated Development Region in South Selangor and in Selangor's continued industrial growth.
"As the development progresses, we look forward to seeing it attract more high-value investments and create quality employment opportunities that will contribute to the state's long-term economic growth," he said.
NSIP is being developed in six phases and is positioned by NCT Alliance as a managed industrial park incorporating digital infrastructure, renewable energy and sustainability features.
Launched in 2023, NSIP is located near the Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Port Klang and the West Coast Expressway, providing access by air, sea and road.
Phases two and three will expand the park's industrial offerings, while subsequent phases are planned to include commercial components such as a petrol station and shop lots.

Title: Malay Education Mobility Index needed to measure outcomes — Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malay Education Mobility Index should be introduced to measure how effectively education improves the capabilities, skills and social mobility of Malays, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said educational success should not be measured solely by access, enrolment, qualifications and tuition, but by how far education develops human capabilities and improves a person's social standing.
"The measure of education cannot stop at access, enrolment, qualifications and tuition. The broader measure is how far education develops human capabilities, drives social mobility and strengthens a nation.
"That is why I propose a Malay Education Mobility Index to track a child's educational journey, from their socioeconomic background and learning achievements to their academic pathway, employment, skills matching and knowledge development," he said in his closing address at the 2026 Malay Education Convention at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.

Title: Engineering must drive resilient, regenerative solutions, says UTP chancellor
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Engineering must move beyond solving today's problems and create resilient, regenerative solutions that safeguard future generations, says Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP) chancellor Tan Sri Dr Mohd Hassan Marican.
He said the role of engineering could no longer be confined to designing systems or developing technologies, particularly amid an unprecedented energy transition, rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and growing global disorder.
"Its purpose must now be to deliver solutions that strengthen resilience in the face of uncertainty while regenerating the natural, economic and social systems upon which future generations will depend," he said.
He said resilience enabled societies to anticipate disruption, absorb shocks and adapt with agility, while regeneration required moving beyond sustaining existing systems to restoring ecosystems, revitalising industries and creating lasting value for society.
He was delivering his welcoming address at the World Engineering, Science and Technology Congress 2026 (ESTCON2026) at the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre today.
Themed "Technology, Resilience and Regeneration: Engineering Pathways to a Sustainable Future", the two-day congress brings together academia, industry and policymakers to exchange ideas and forge cross-disciplinary collaborations.
Hassan said the theme was timely as the world faced intensifying great-power rivalry, regional conflicts, trade fragmentation and the rapid proliferation of AI, alongside the energy transition.
He said UTP's strategic direction centred on three Grand Challenges: Energy Security, Sustainable Living and Regenerative Futures, which guide its education, research, investments and partnerships.
As Petronas' knowledge partner, UTP was supporting the energy company's transformation through research and talent development in cleaner energy, carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, renewable energy, digitalisation and emissions reduction.
"Tomorrow's engineers must not only be technically proficient, but also have the wisdom to apply technology responsibly and the adaptability to thrive and lead in a rapidly changing world," he said.
He said the scale and complexity of today's challenges meant breakthroughs could not be achieved in isolation.
He urged delegates to challenge established perspectives, exchange knowledge and pursue partnerships based on trust to deliver purposeful innovation for communities, nations and the world.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kalimantan forest fires cause severe haze, water shortages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prolonged forest and peatland fires in South Kalimantan have degraded air quality and caused acute water shortages due to dry weather.
Kota Banjar resident and local representative Muhammad Adi Maulana Noor, better known as Adi van der Pijl, said hazy conditions in several areas were severe enough to disrupt daily routines, especially in the mornings.
He said the situation had also impacted the education sector, forcing the closure of several schools.
"In South Kalimantan, hotspots are extremely widespread, reaching roughly between 60,000 and 70,000.
"Conditions here remain dry, well water levels have dropped significantly.
Residents struggle to obtain water," he told Bernama TV's Fokus 15 programme, titled 'Jerebu Kalimantan, Semakin Mengusarkan', today.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Adi said efforts by the Indonesian government to induce rain through cloud seeding to alleviate the drought have not yielded results, with no rainfall recorded so far.
He said that recurring fires during the dry season require a more comprehensive approach, including a fair assessment of root causes rather than placing sole blame on smallholders managing small-scale farms.
"The fires cover vast areas spanning thousands of hectares. Smallholders working on small plots actually have the experience to manage small fires," he said.
Commenting on the impact of transboundary haze, Muhammad Adi emphasised the importance of formulating a concrete action plan to ensure the crisis is addressed effectively in the future. — BERNAMA

Title: TH RCI: Former minister released on MACC bail

Title: Low risk of Anak Krakatau volcanic ash reaching Malaysia, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shifting wind patterns and potential subsequent eruptions could influence the movement of volcanic ash from Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau towards Malaysia, though current risk levels remain low.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said analysis of current wind speed, direction, and volcanic ash monitoring indicates a low probability of the ash reaching Malaysia.
He said the ash dispersion is currently concentrated around the Sunda Strait and adjacent regions in Indonesia.
"MetMalaysia will continue to monitor the situation using satellite data and atmospheric analysis," he said when contacted today.
"Information from the global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC) will also enable us to detect any potential ash movement into Malaysian airspace and notify the public promptly."
Earlier, media reported that ongoing eruptions from Mount Anak Krakatau since Friday produced volcanic ash plumes that forced six airports to suspend flight operations.
The disruption affected domestic and international flights, including routes connecting Jakarta with Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul/Incheon, Doha, and Amsterdam.
Commenting on the potential impact should the ash reach Malaysia, he said the primary threat would be disruptions to domestic and international flight operations.
He said volcanic eruptions are monitored by the VAAC under the purview of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).
"Should incoming information indicate potential impacts on Malaysian airspace, MetMalaysia will issue volcanic ash warnings or advisories to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), airline operators, and airport managers," he said.
Hisham also clarified that the current low visibility experienced in parts of Sarawak and the western peninsula is caused by transboundary haze, not volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina supports tougher scam penalties, but says banks must share responsibility
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said supports the police proposal for heavier penalties, including caning, for online scammers.
However, she said efforts to curb online scams should not focus solely on harsher punishment, as financial institutions must also play their part and take greater responsibility.
"I have seen their proposal to introduce caning, and I can agree with going beyond caning for scam-related offences," she told reporters after officiating the 2026 Political Funding Convention at the Asian International Arbitration Centre today.
"I have said many times in and outside Parliament that one strategy is for banks receiving scam proceeds to also take responsibility."
Azalina said it was unfair for banks to place the full burden of losses caused by scams on customers on the grounds that their accounts had been misused by others.
"It cannot be that when someone uses a victim's bank account, the bank simply says, 'It's at your own risk'. In that case, people might as well keep their money under their mattresses," she said.
"Bank Negara Malaysia has issued numerous public service announcements, and the police have repeatedly warned the public, yet people continue to fall victim to scams."
Azalina said the government must assess whether harsher penalties would genuinely reduce scam cases or whether a mechanism imposing shared responsibility on banks would be more effective in tackling the crime.
She added that greater accountability would encourage financial institutions to strengthen their monitoring and security systems to prevent suspicious transactions.
Yesterday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the police had proposed amendments to outdated laws and significantly tougher penalties, including caning, for online scammers.
Khalid said the penalties currently imposed by the courts were
too lenient
to deter masterminds and members of scam syndicates.

Title: Johor launches week-long operation to capture 5 dogs that mauled toddler
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor has launched a week-long operation to track down and capture five stray dogs that mauled a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat, on Saturday.
State Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said the dogs must be captured and tested for rabies, with the operation to be intensified for at least a week.
He said ruling out rabies was crucial not only for the safety of residents but also to ease concerns over
Nur Haira Wafiqah
Muhammad Hamizi's recovery.
"The hospital is also concerned about whether the dogs that attacked the child were carrying rabies.
"Immediate action is therefore needed to capture and examine the dogs. If they are confirmed to be rabies-free, it will give some relief to the doctors and her parents, as this concern could affect the child's recovery," he said.
Fared said the operation involved the Batu Pahat district office, Department Veterinary Services (DVS) and police, with various lawful methods to be deployed to locate the dogs.
"We will not rely on a single method. Surveillance, monitoring and intelligence-gathering will be intensified, including any methods permitted by law.
"Our commitment is to resolve the stray dog problem in the area and prevent a similar incident from happening to others," he said.
He said the Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) and DVS had previously conducted operations on Aug 12, 26 and 30, resulting in 22 stray dogs being captured in the area.
However, the continued presence of stray dogs showed that capture efforts needed to be stepped up and carried out continuously, he said.
Fared said the state government would fully cover Nur Haira's medical treatment and rehabilitation costs, with the toddler expected to undergo a lengthy recovery.
He also urged the hospital to pay close attention to the emotional wellbeing of the family, particularly Nur Haira's
12-year-old brother
, who remains traumatised after witnessing the attack.
Fared said this after visiting Nur Haira, who remains sedated and under treatment at the paediatric intensive care unit of Sultanah Aminah Hospital today.

Title: Civil servants on boards must be active, voice views, says Chief Secretary
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Government-appointed board members must actively strengthen governance and accountability rather than merely attend meetings, said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
He said civil servants appointed to board positions must play an active role, voice professional views courageously, and evaluate every proposal thoroughly.
"Strengthening governance, accountability, and compliance must remain a priority to ensure weaknesses and non-compliance are identified and addressed at the earliest stage, thereby reducing the risks of corruption and abuse of power," Shamsul Azri said when chairing the National Governance Committee Meeting Series 8 at the Prime Minister's Department yesterday.
"They cannot be passive observers because every decision made is a collective responsibility that must be defended in the best interests of the organisation and the nation."
Shamsul Azri said views, reprimands, or concerns raised by civil servants during board meetings must be recorded clearly in the meeting minutes.
He said proper records serve as official references and ensure that an officer's stance can be identified should questions arise over decisions made.
At the meeting, Shamsul Azri proposed that 36 research findings on integrity and anti-corruption presented at the Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference from 2022 to 2025 be brought to the Special Task Force on Agency Reform meeting.
He said the findings should be distributed to all government agencies as reference material for drafting policies and strategies related to governance, integrity, and anti-corruption.
"The research findings can help identify weaknesses and areas for improvement, continuously strengthening the government's anti-corruption, governance, and integrity efforts," he added.
Also present were Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz, Auditor-General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi, and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy chief commissioner (Prevention) Datuk Azmi Kamaruzaman, alongside MACC directors.

Article:

Title: Boy, 12, tried to rescue sister from five stray dogs
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 12-year-old boy remains traumatised after witnessing his 2-year-old sister being mauled by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat, on Saturday.
His mother, Nur Wahyuni Harun, 36, said her second child had tried to chase the dogs away after seeing the pack attack Nur Haira Wafiqah Muhammad Hamizi.
She said the ordeal had left the boy emotionally shaken, with his older sister telling her that he had broken down in tears several times while recalling the attack.
"When I called to ask if he was okay, his sister said he was crying. Perhaps even when he closes his eyes, he remembers what happened.
"I am here while he is in Batu Pahat. I cannot even hug him. My husband and I have also lost our appetite, and he is not eating either."
Nur Wahyuni said Nur Haira had suffered severe injuries, particularly to her head and cheek, besides wounds across much of her body.
"Several wounds on her back were stitched after her first surgery. Doctors are still monitoring her condition before proceeding with the next procedure," she said.
Recounting the incident, Nur Wahyuni said she and her husband, Mohamad Hamizi Hamdan, 37, a maintenance worker, had left their home in Batu Pahat at 6.50am to travel to Johor Baru for business before receiving a call about their daughter being attacked.
"We received the call at 7.20am and immediately turned back.
"I am devastated because it happened on my birthday," she said.
At about 7am, Nur Haira was found covered in blood after being attacked by the five dogs outside her home. She suffered severe injuries to her head and cheek.
The
attack
was noticed by her grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, 56, who screamed for help after seeing the dogs surrounding the toddler.
Earlier today, Johor Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled visited Nur Haira at the intensive care unit of Sultanah Aminah Hospital.

Title: Kwasa Damansara set for population boom, expects 100,000 residents [WATCH]
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Kwasa Land Sdn Bhd expects the population of its 912.57-hectare Kwasa Damansara township to reach about 100,000 within the next five years as more residential projects are completed.
Managing director Datuk Adenan Md Yusof said new developments, including almost 2,000 affordable housing units nearing completion and another 4,000 units planned in the next phase, would support the population growth.
"We are expecting about 100,000 population in five years to come," he said during the Kwasa Damansara media day and site tour today.
Adenan said the first phase of the affordable housing development was almost complete and expected to be delivered by year-end.
The second phase of about 4,000 units was also expected to begin by year-end.
"If you multiply that by three, in terms of population, that is already 6,000. Phase 2 development, another 4,000 units, is also coming soon by year-end," he said.
Adenan also highlighted an upcoming development known as Seri Damansara, comprising about 200 high-end condominium units.
He said the units were expected to be priced at about RM900,000 to RM1 million, with the development expected to come on stream by the end of 2027.
The township, which spans parts of Shah Alam and Petaling Jaya, is seeing completed neighbourhoods alongside projects under construction and new residential developments.
Adenan said the township's residential offering would comprise a mix of landed and high-density developments to cater to different segments of the market.
One of the developments is Daya Residence, a 260-unit freehold, low-density project by TSR Development Sdn Bhd.
Developed across two phases, Daya Residence comprises 34 semi-detached homes, one bungalow, seven town villas and 218 condominium units.
Other residential projects include Dedaun Rimba, a completed 264-unit development by YTL Land & Development Bhd, and Linari, which is under construction with 496 units and scheduled for completion in 2028.
Tujuh Residences by Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd offers 573 residences within the 25.9-hectare Kwasa Damansara City Centre, while RIA Residensi by Sunsuria will comprise 520 units across a 3.85-hectare site.
Waringin, another recent residential addition, comprises 820 homes across 8.53 hectares and will be delivered in two phases.
Meanwhile, Kwasa Land is targeting wider housing accessibility through Idaman Kwasa Damansara, with its first phase comprising 1,669 homes across 5.63 hectares.
The development is targeted for completion in 2027 and has received more than 3,400 approved applicants.
Kwasa Land is also targeting wider housing accessibility through Idaman Kwasa Damansara, with its first phase comprising 1,669 affordable homes.
The project forms part of a wider plan to deliver 11,000 affordable homes across the township and has received more than 3,400 approved applicants.
"At the end of the day, we want Kwasa Damansara to serve a broad cross-section of Malaysians.
"Quality homes, connectivity and access to community amenities should not be limited to only one segment of society," said Adenan.
Kwasa Damansara is planned as a transit-oriented development served by two MRT stations, Kwasa Damansara and Kwasa Sentral.
The township is also connected to six major road and expressway networks, including the Damansara-Shah Alam Elevated Expressway, North Klang Valley Expressway and Guthrie Corridor Expressway.
Around 912.57-hectare, or 11 per cent of the township have been allocated for parks, landscaped areas and other green and open spaces.
Meanwhile, Kwasa Damansara City Centre is emerging as the township's commercial hub, while Urban Eats next to Menara KWSP currently houses nine food, beverage and retail operators.
Adenan said development would continue progressively according to infrastructure readiness, market conditions and community requirements.
"The progress we are seeing today reflects the deliberate and phased approach required to develop a township of this scale.
"Each component must contribute to the wider township ecosystem. Our role is not simply to deliver individual developments, but to ensure that they come together to create a connected, active and liveable community over the long term.
"We are moving from masterplan to reality, and from individual developments towards a more complete township experience," said Adenan.

Title: Bumiputera education must move beyond quotas towards self-reliance - Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The future of education for the Malay and Bumiputera communities must move beyond quotas towards greater self-reliance and resilience.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the success of the communities should instead be measured by their ability to excel in critical fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), develop new technologies and own intellectual property.
"The measure is not only the number of students entering university, but how many can think critically, master STEM, build global companies and lead world-class institutions," he said when launching the Malay Education Convention 2026 today.
Zambry said that to achieve this goal, the country's education ecosystem needed to move beyond simply providing access towards improving quality, building competencies, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing from technology use to technology ownership.
He said Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) should no longer be viewed as a second choice, but as a key pathway for developing national talent and producing highly skilled technicians and problem-solving experts.
Addressing the narrative of Bumiputera dependency, Zambry said affirmative policies remained relevant as long as structural imbalances persisted, but their ultimate objective must be to empower the Bumiputera community to achieve excellence and become independent.
"Malay and Bumiputera education cannot forever be built on the narrative that 'we need to be helped because we are weak'.
"The narrative of the future must be: 'We are given the opportunity to become strong, stand on our own, lead and help others'," he said.
He said mastery of the Malay language was important as a language of knowledge and identity, while proficiency in English and other languages was essential to competing globally without compromising integrity.
"In the pursuit of global excellence, we must never lose our identity and values. Education must produce not only intelligent people, but individuals of good character, integrity and the moral courage to lead," he said.
On the convention, which is a continuation of the Bumiputera Education Congress held on May 1, Zambry said it would culminate in the formulation of a comprehensive resolution.
He said the resolution would subsequently be submitted to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi for consideration and further policy action by the government.

Title: Why the Malacca Strait demands a binding Asean security framework
Article:
ON July 11, 1882, British warships anchored off Alexandria and unleashed a devastating barrage on the city's fortifications. The pretext was "restoring order" and "protecting the Suez Canal."
Within weeks, General Garnet Wolseley's forces crushed the Egyptian army at Tel elKebir, turning the Khedive into a puppet.
The reality was far uglier: London forcibly seized Egypt's fiscal sovereignty, diverted its vast cotton revenues to European bondholders, and transformed a proud civilisation into a debt colony – bled dry so that Lancashire's mills could spin and British shareholders could prosper.
Fast forward to Aug 29, 2026. President Donald Trump announces a deal for a "huge US stake" in Venezuela's 65 billion barrel petroleum reserves.
But this is no negotiation between equals. It is the 1882 playbook, republished with American firepower.
If might alone can seize the resources of the weak, then every international contract, every shipping lane, and every digital transaction becomes a hostage to raw force.
Nowhere is this lesson more urgent than in Southeast Asia. The world has watched the Strait of Hormuz with bated breath, recognising that any disruption there sends oil prices soaring and economies reeling.
But we must take that warning and apply it to our own backyard – because the Strait of Malacca is equally, if not more, critical to the survival of globalisation.
Over 90,000 vessels transit the Malacca Strait annually, carrying roughly 40 per cent of global maritime trade and nearly 80 per cent of East Asia's oil imports – an annual cargo value exceeding US$5 trillion.
That makes it the world's most important economic funnel.
But goods are only half the story. Most people do not realise that the seabed of the Malacca Strait hosts one of the densest concentrations of submarine fibreoptic cables on Earth.
These slender glass threads carry approximately 95 per cent of the world's communications – 99 per cent of all transcontinental digital traffic.
Now imagine the unthinkable: a hostile warship decides to park at the entrance of this 2.8km wide funnel.
It does not need to fire a single shot. By merely anchoring there, it could halt shipping, disrupt cable repair operations, and effectively hold the economies of China, India, Japan, and all of Southeast Asia hostage.
Half the region could go digitally dark in minutes.
Financial markets would freeze. Supply chains would shatter. Hospitals would lose telemedicine; airports would lose flight coordination; governments would lose the ability to move money.
This is not hyperbole; it is the new reality of great power competition, unfolding right on our doorstep.
That is why Asean must rise to the occasion and do more. We cannot afford to be passive spectators while the giants circle our waters.
The good news is that we have practical, working mechanisms for cooperative security among the littoral states such as the Malacca Straits Patrol (MSP). But they are not enough.
Today's threats demand a broader, more institutionalised framework.
Asean must upgrade and multilateralise these local initiatives under the umbrella of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC) , transforming ad hoc operational cooperation into a binding strategic commitment with explicit protocols for protecting both shipping and submarine cables.
[[nid:1528211]]
This is precisely where the TAC becomes indispensable. This year marks its 50th anniversary – a treaty whose core principles include mutual respect, noninterference, peaceful dispute settlement, and the renunciation of force.
The TAC today has grown beyond its region to include 62 member states – almost a third of the entire United Nations, including major powers such as Germany, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, the United States, China, and Iran.
Remarkably all the principal antagonists in today's geopolitical rivalries have voluntarily subscribed to this single Asian framework of strategic restraint.
The US and China, Washington and Teheran – they have all signed the same pledge to settle disputes peacefully.
This is a historic moment – an unprecedented opportunity for Asean to play a consequential global role.
We have the venue, the treaty, and the membership. What we lack is the political will to transform the TAC from a diplomatic document into a living regional compact for crisis management.
Crucially, the machinery to do so already exists in the treaty's own text. Article 14 of the TAC explicitly provides for the constitution of a High Council – a continuing body "to take cognizance of the existence of disputes or situations likely to disturb regional peace and harmony".
Article 15 empowers the High Council to recommend appropriate means of settlement – good offices, mediation, inquiry, or conciliation – and to recommend measures to prevent the deterioration of a dispute.
Yet, remarkably, in five decades, the High Council has never been formally invoked. The mechanism sits on the shelf while the world around it grows more dangerous.
Asean must finally activate it – not as a crisis afterthought, but as a standing, credible forum for de-escalation and trust building.
Asean should use this golden anniversary to operationalise the TAC in concrete ways. We need joint maritime surveillance and real time incident hotlines among the littoral states – Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand – including explicit protocols for protecting submarine cables from both physical and hybrid threats.
We need a neutral, Asean chaired arbitration mechanism so that any dispute over transit, military presence, or cable integrity is settled around a table, not at the barrel of a gun.
And we need a clear collective commitment that no external power will be granted unilateral "policing" rights over our waters – a commitment that the MSP was originally designed to forestall when the United States proposed policing the strait in the early 2000s.
Our strategic objective must be clear: build enough regional resilience that Southeast Asia remains peaceful and autonomous even when the great powers become unpredictable.
If we succeed, Southeast Asia becomes a model for the Global Majority – proof that we can collectively defend our sovereignty without surrendering to any empire.
* The writer is chairman of Citizens International, a civil society organisation based in Penang dedicated to internationalism, peaceful coexistence and global cooperation for a better world

Title: Selangor on track to smash RM80bil investment target, eyes RM100bil
Article:
SEPANG: Selangor is confident of surpassing its RM80 billion investment target this year and potentially setting a new record of more than RM100 billion, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the state had secured RM70 billion in investments by the middle of 2026, putting it on track to exceed the target.
"We have a target of RM80 billion, in line with the achievement in 2025. But by the middle of 2026, we have reached RM70 billion, and that is the biggest in Malaysia.
"With that trend, we believe that we can reach RM80 billion. In fact, if the trend remains good, we believe that we can set a record of more than RM100 billion," he told reporters at NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP) today.
Amirudin said Selangor recorded RM33 billion-RM34 billion in investments in the first quarter, before reaching RM70 billion by the second quarter.
He said the state will continue its business missions overseas to attract investments, with the Invest Selangor team scheduled to visit France and Berlin in September.
"We also try to go abroad. In September, the Invest Selangor team will go to France. We will also go to Berlin. Previously, we went to Korea and other places," he said.
Amirudin said Selangor's consistent strategy had helped maintain its investment momentum, noting that the state recorded RM80 billion in investments last year and more than RM100 billion the year before.
He said the outlook would also be supported by developments in industrial areas, including NSIP and Bukit Raja in Klang, as well as other areas.

Title: MetMalaysia: Malaysia could see temperatures hit 40°C from January to May 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia could experience extreme heat and dry weather from January to May next year, with temperatures in some areas potentially reaching 40°C as a very strong El Nino, or Super El Nino, is expected to develop towards the end of this year.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the likelihood of the phenomenon occurring was now approaching 100 per cent, based on climate model forecasts from international observation and research centres, according to a report published by
Berita Harian
.
He said past meteorological records showed that very strong El Nino episodes were often associated with higher temperatures, dry weather and a serious risk of haze, similar to conditions currently affecting the country.
“Experience from the Super El Nino episodes of 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 showed that the country’s daily maximum temperatures at the time were more extreme than during other periods.
“The country recorded its highest temperature of 40.1°C at the Chuping Meteorological Station in Perlis on April 9, 1998, and 39.3°C at the Batu Embun Meteorological Station in Jerantut, Pahang on April 10, 2016,” he said.
Mohd Hisham said there was about a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the current El Nino would exceed the strength of any El Nino episode recorded since 1950.
“The situation could cause northern and inland areas of the peninsula, as well as inland Sabah and Sarawak, to record higher-than-usual temperatures and increase the risk of hot weather and heatwaves from the end of the North-east Monsoon in January until May 2027.
“Based on the latest projections, more meteorological stations in the northern peninsula could record temperatures of up to 40°C during the peak of the hot season between January and May 2027,” he said.
He warned that rising temperatures and prolonged hot weather could increase the risk of heatwaves and affect health, particularly among children, the elderly and those engaging in outdoor activities.
“Reduced rainfall and longer dry periods could put pressure on water resources, including catchment areas and dams, while also affecting agriculture and other industries sensitive to water shortages.
“Prolonged hot and dry conditions would also make vegetation more susceptible to fires, increasing the risk of forest and peatland fires as well as haze, both locally and across borders,” he said.

Title: Senior medical officer in Melaka remanded over RM1.5m knee implant supply probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 —  A senior medical officer has been remanded for five days to assist a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into alleged abuse of position involving the supply of knee implants worth about RM1.5 million.
The remand order for the man, in his 50s, was issued by Ayer Keroh Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman at the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court in Melaka this morning,
Harian Metro
reported.
The public servant has been remanded until September 12 after MACC applied for the order to facilitate further investigations.
According to a source, the suspect was detained at about 3.30pm yesterday after he arrived at the Melaka MACC office to give a statement.
The source said preliminary investigations found that the suspect was believed to have committed the alleged offence between 2024 and 2026.

Title: Anwar to chair MA63 meeting on Sabah’s 40pc revenue claim, says Hajiji
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Sabah’s claim for 40 per cent of its net revenue will be among the issues discussed at a Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) meeting to be chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim this Friday.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said Sabah would host the meeting, which would also discuss outstanding claims and issues under MA63,
Sinar Harian
reported.
He said this after a working visit to the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant in Kunak today.
Hajiji said the Sabah government was grateful to Anwar, as nine matters under MA63 had been resolved during his administration, including the devolution of certain powers to Sabah.
“Previously there were four matters, so a total of 13 (matters) have been resolved. However, there are still other matters, including the 40 per cent payment,” he said.
Hajiji said the federal government had agreed to Sabah’s claim for the 40 per cent payment, but several technical issues remained to be resolved.
“They have agreed but there are still some issues, perhaps technical issues, that have been raised. This is a normal process because there is an appeal process, but it does not affect the decision for us to receive the 40 per cent payment,” he said.
He said unresolved matters would be raised again for consideration at subsequent MA63 meetings or negotiations.
In a separate development, Hajiji welcomed progress on the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant, which is nearing completion and is expected to begin producing vitamin E before the end of the year.
He said the plant represented a positive development and a downstream business for Sawit Kinabalu Group, using palm-based materials in its production.
“I am very pleased to hear the briefing from Sawit Kinabalu and the company working with Sawit Kinabalu that the plant built to produce vitamin E is almost completed and will produce vitamin E before the end of the year,” he said.
Hajiji said the project was believed to be the first of its kind in Malaysia and could help increase revenue for Sawit Kinabalu and its partner company.

Title: Former minister released on MACC bail over Tabung Haji RCI probe, chief commissioner confirms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — A former minister who was remanded over an investigation linked to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail today.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the release,
Sinar Harian
reported today.
“He (the former minister) has been released on MACC bail,” he said today.
The man, in his 60s, was initially remanded for five days from September 2 to 6 before his remand was extended by another two days until today.
The former lawmaker was detained after he appeared at the MACC headquarters here on September 2 to give a statement and was investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The RCI report, which was made public on July 29, contained 25 key recommendations aimed at improving transparency, professionalism and governance at the institution.
Among the recommendations was a proposal to bar active politicians from serving on the TH board to prevent political interference.
Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim had also called for investigations into the findings of the TH RCI to be pursued “to the ends of the earth”.

Title: Should political party donors be protected? Azalina says issue among those being studied
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — If Malaysia were to have a law regulating donations to political parties, should it protect donors from being pursued by anti-corruption investigators after donating money?
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that this was among the technical issues that have to be studied before steps are taken to introduce a political financing law in Malaysia.
Azalina today listed nine parameters or areas of the proposed political financing law that are currently being fine-tuned, including who the law will cover; the supervisory body; the source and limits of donations; prohibition on foreign donations; traceable ways of receiving funds; reporting, auditing and disclosure; and offences and penalties.
At a press conference here, Azalina gave examples of issues that still have to be considered under the proposed law, including foreign donors.
Azalina said some countries, for example, prohibit foreigners from donating, while others have procedures requiring foreign donors to disclose their donations.
“Secondly, when you donate, will you be subjected to income tax deduction, or you must inform the source of your money? If everyone who donates have to inform the source of the money, maybe when will not want to donate,” she said at a press conference after the Political Financing Convention 2026.
Noting that some people might donate to all political parties as a form of “buying insurance”, Azalina said another issue to be considered was whether the law would allow donors to contribute to more than one political party.
She added that there was a possibility that no one would want to donate to political parties if such a law were introduced.
“And fourthly, do we want to make sure that when people donate, MACC won’t come and disturb, ‘why you donate?’” she said.
Later, when speaking on the same point, Azalina said she personally felt that political parties could issue receipts to donors, but said it had to be studied whether “to give protection to donors”, as donors might be deterred from donating if they were pursued after making donations.
“But we must give protection to donors also. If not, who will want to donate right?” she said at another point.
“But I agree if it’s a foreign donor, we must have a certain process. There must be a procedure, whether select committee or Parliament is informed, because if a foreign donor wants to influence our decision, this is also a problem right,” she said.
Azalina had explained that the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) had been carrying out engagement studies and surveys over the past two years.
Azalina today urged BHEUU to obtain written official views from political parties on whether they agreed with having a political financing law in Malaysia.
After that, Azalina said the proposed law would be brought to the Cabinet for evaluation from multiple perspectives.
She told the media that the Cabinet would then decide on the final “format” of the technical aspects of the proposed law before the Bill is brought to Parliament to be voted on.
Earlier, when speaking as minister in a speech at the same convention, Azalina said the government’s goal was not just to draft laws, but to ensure they were truly effective and capable of being implemented.
She had spoken of the simple principle of being “transparent but practical, stern but fair, and accountability without curbing the legitimate democratic process”.
Today, Azalina, when giving her personal opinion as a lawyer and MP, said politicians could easily find themselves being charged with corruption if there is no political funding law in Malaysia to regulate donations to them.
