Title: Nazir Razak, Musa Hitam say NEP fostered ‘tongkat culture’ among Malays
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The New Economic Policy (NEP) fostered a culture of dependency among Malays and became too focused on ownership and government assistance, former CIMB Group chairman Tan Sri Nazir Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Musa Hitam said today.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that the two made the remarks at a forum titled “Remembering Tun Abdul Razak: Architect of Malaysia’s Development and Nation Building”, which discussed whether the NEP should be reviewed, replaced or remodelled.
Nazir said the NEP was intended to run for only 20 years and cited former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman’s description of it as a 20-year “handicap”.
“We will be in serious trouble if we have to continue. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” said Nazir, the son of second prime minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.
He said the policy should be reviewed, with greater emphasis placed on education and professional development instead of the distribution of shares and ownership.
“The NEP focused too much on the distribution of shares and ownership. And when you go down that path, all these ‘Ali Babas’ come up,” he said, referring to a culture of rent-seeking.
“I think we focused on the wrong theme in the execution of the NEP,” he added.
Nazir also questioned the practice of awarding contracts to Bumiputera businesses, particularly why politicians were allowed to choose the recipients.
“They (politicians) don’t want competition among Bumiputeras,” he said, adding that the lack of competition had weakened Bumiputera businesses.
Musa, who served as deputy prime minister from 1981 to 1986, said the policy had also made Malays overly reliant on government assistance.
“To me, the economic policy for the Malays has caused the Malays to become too pampered. Pampered by the government,” he said.
Musa said the NEP had benefited Malays and the country as a whole, but had also created a sense of insecurity, with recipients continuing to feel that government assistance was insufficient.
“People fear receiving nothing, but even when they receive assistance, they say it is not enough and ask for more.”

Title: Did the Negeri Sembilan MB sign decree to oust ruler? Claim sees state in renewed palace crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Negeri Sembilan has been thrust again into its unprecedented constitutional crisis, with claims that new Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim allegedly signed a proclamation to depose the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, just one day after swearing an oath of allegiance to him.
According to
The Straits Times
, the explosive allegation was made public in a September 5 statement by the state’s four traditional ruling chieftains, the Undang Yang Empat, who possess customary authority under Adat Perpatih to elect and — they claim — dismiss the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
When pressed on the allegations on September 6, Ismail did not directly deny signing the decree, stating only that “the four Undang have the right to their opinion” while reaffirming that he “and the state government express full loyalty to Muhriz Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar”.
The standoff is the most recent escalation yet in a months-long palace conflict that could colour Malaysian politics ahead of key elections.
According to the statement released by the four chieftains, Ismail met them on August 3 alongside throne contender Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, the cousin of Tuanku Muhriz and son of the previous ruler.
The chieftains alleged that Ismail signed the formal proclamation ousting Tuanku Muhriz during this gathering, paving the way for Tuanku Nadzaruddin’s installation.
Sources told
The Straits Times
that the private meeting was attended by top Umno leaders, including party president and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
All three reportedly declined requests for comment.
However, legal and government sources told
The Straits Times
that Ismail has privately claimed he was coerced into signing the document under severe political duress, alleging that Umno’s central leadership orchestrated the manoeuvre alongside the chieftains.
The same sources indicated that Ismail is preparing to lodge an official police report regarding the incident today.
Despite the purported signing on August 3, Ismail proceeded to swear in his state executive council before Tuanku Muhriz four days later on August 7, entrenching an extraordinary constitutional contradiction.
This development will again put the spotlight on Umno’s role in the Negeri Sembilan constitutional crisis.
Ahead of last month’s state election, Umno’s state lawmakers had withdrawn support for the menteri besar at the time, Datuk Seri Aminudin Harun, ostensibly for his public support of Tuanku Muhriz in the public row with the four Undang, before suddenly reversing this position.
Umno had sought to mitigate this prior to the election by positioning itself as a “mediator” to resolve the royal crisis.
“This is about crisis management. It’s how you manage the crisis. That is why the rakyat must consider all factors before they decide,” said Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, one of the key personalities in the move to oust Aminudin

Title: Fahmi: Govt agencies to work together to tighten e-commerce rules, curb sale of prohibited goods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Communications Ministry is prepared to work with the Home Ministry, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, police and relevant agencies to strengthen e-commerce regulation and curb the sale of prohibited goods, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said such cooperation was important as there were still gaps in the country’s e-commerce ecosystem, particularly as e-commerce platforms are currently not subject to licensing.
“There are indeed gaps in the e-commerce system. At present, e-commerce is not yet licensed, so we need to look into this matter,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the Huawei WAIC Connect Malaysia 2026 Symposium today.
Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had held a meeting with a major platform yesterday, but he had yet to receive an update on the outcome of the meeting as of this morning.
He said most e-commerce platforms in Malaysia prohibit the sale of prohibited products, including drugs such as fentanyl, but expressed concern that one platform appeared to be too lax in allowing such products to be offered.
“The accounts selling these prohibited products may be fake accounts,” he said.
Fahmi stressed that platforms needed to address the issue of fake accounts being created and the sale of prohibited products, rather than merely removing search keywords, which could make such products harder to find without addressing the actual problem.
“That should not be the way,” he said, adding that platforms needed to prevent fake accounts from being created for the purpose of selling drugs.
Previously, MCMC was instructed to hold meetings with e-commerce platforms following concerns over the online sale of drugs, including fentanyl and a substance referred to as “piu-piu”.
Fahmi said he had received a message from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim regarding the phenomenon, which was seen as increasingly worrying. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: Malaysians want political funding law before GE16; political parties’ buy-in needed to avoid delay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysians have voiced their desire for Malaysia to have a political financing law to regulate political parties’ funding before the 16th general election, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today.
Azalina’s remarks were based on findings from the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) public engagement sessions.
“I was informed by the BHEUU deputy director general (policy) many voices of the public wants, if possible, that this Act can be in force before the 16th general election,” she said at the Political Financing Convention 2026 held at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) building.
Azalina said the views of political parties would have to be obtained before the proposed political financing law is brought to Parliament, as it would be politicians in Parliament who would vote on whether to introduce such a law.
“So they are the users and they will vote on the law. So you must have them to have more say. If not, the delay of the Act may happen if there is no buy-in from political parties,” she said.
Earlier in the same speech, Azalina said she understood the debates, criticism and public anxiety over the process to introduce a political financing law not being as quick as other reform agendas.
“And certainly the people have the right to hope for changes and to demand the government fulfill the commitment as soon as possible.
“But on behalf of the government, I admit that the agenda of institutional legal reform, when we talk about political financing, is not a process that is that simple and capable of being implemented so quickly,” she said, emphasising the need for political parties to be stakeholders and to give their views since the proposed law would apply to them.
“Political will is not just measured by how quickly a reform is presented, but it also has to be evaluated based on the courage to start it, the readiness to accept views and criticism, and the strength of determination to carry it out,” she added.
Earlier in the speech, Azalina said BHEUU had taken over studies on the proposed political financing law since May 2023, and that the Cabinet had on September 8, 2023 agreed in principle to the drafting of the law and decided on further studies on the policy scope.
Azalina noted that BHEUU had carried out engagement work on the proposed law reform over the past two years.
Later at a press conference, Azalina replied to a question on why the political financing law had yet to be introduced in Malaysia, saying this was due to studies being carried out over the past two years: “The delay is not a political delay, but delay in terms of process and procedure done by BHEUU.”
Asked if it was possible for the proposed political financing law to be introduced before GE16, Azalina said the question of when GE16 would be held should be directed to the prime minister.
As for the timeline for how soon the law could be introduced, Azalina said, “I wish it’s as soon as possible”, but that it would depend on the work being done to prepare the Bill.
At the press conference, Azalina outlined various technical aspects of the proposed political financing law that have to be considered before it is brought to the Cabinet, and also proposed that BHEUU collect the written official opinions of all registered political parties in Malaysia on whether they agree to such a law.
Findings show 90.3 per cent want political financing law before GE16
Earlier at the convention, BHEUU deputy director-general (policy and development) Datuk Punitha Silivarajoo presented the findings from BHEUU’s engagement involving 1,544 participants nationwide in 12 engagement sessions from June to November 2025.
Punitha said 100 per cent of the 1,544 participants agreed that Malaysia needs to have a political financing law, and that 90.3 per cent of the 1,544 wanted this law to be tabled and passed in Parliament before the next general election.
Out of the 1,544 participants, 67 per cent were political parties and grassroots leaders, 17 per cent were government agencies and academics, 11 per cent were non-governmental organisations (NGOs), civil society organisations (CSOs) and youths, and five per cent were from the business sector.
A total of 32 political parties and 69 NGOs and CSOs were consulted in the engagement sessions with 1,544 participants.

Title: Lim Guan Eng hits PAS over failure to credit him for cutting lottery draws from 22 to eight a year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at PAS over what he described as dishonest and hypocritical claims about DAP’s position on Islam, while pointing to his record of reducing special lottery draws when he was finance minister.
In a Facebook post, Lim said PAS had failed to acknowledge that he was the first finance minister to reduce the number of special lottery draws from 22 to eight a year when Pakatan Harapan (PH) was in government from 2018 to 2020.
“PAS is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year during the PH government from 2018 to 2020,” he said.
Lim said the number of special draws was subsequently increased to 22 a year by the PAS, Umno, Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) coalition government in 2020 and remained at that level until the BN/PN administration ended in late 2022.
He said PAS did not have to praise him for the policy, but questioned its repeated claims that DAP leaders were opposed to Islam.
“Not praising me is fine, but the question is why does PAS like to slander DAP leaders as being against Islam when DAP is only opposed to PAS and their politics of hatred and lies,” he said.
Lim said it was up to the public to decide whether PAS’ approach amounted to hypocrisy and violated its own principles.
“It is up to the people to determine whether PAS’ two-faced political game violates principles and is hypocritical,” he said.

Title: IBS classrooms to ease overcrowding in Melaka schools, says deputy education minister
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 8 — The construction of additional classrooms using the Industrialised Building System (IBS) will enable special rooms currently used as temporary teaching and learning spaces to resume their original functions, said Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh.
He said the move would help ease overcrowding while enabling schools to make better use of their existing facilities.
“Some schools have had to convert special rooms, including music rooms and laboratories, into classrooms.
“With this construction, the special rooms can once again be used for their intended purposes,” he told reporters after visiting Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Taman Merdeka here today.
According to Wong, 53 schools in Melaka had benefited from the construction of additional classrooms using IBS, 49 of which had more than 35 students per class.
He said three schools in the Kesidang state constituency, namely SK Malim, SK Taman Merdeka and SK Tengkera 1, had received a total allocation of RM3.3 million to construct 11 additional classrooms under the initiative, with completion expected by December 2026.
“The additional classroom construction projects at the three schools are currently around 40 per cent complete and are expected to be completed before the 2027 school session begins,” he said.
Commenting on the double-cohort intake for Year One in the 2027 school session, Wong said 416,632 pupils had so far registered in the seven-year-old cohort, while 73,487 had registered in the six-year-old cohort.
On teacher readiness, he said the Ministry of Education (MOE) had taken several measures, including placing Institute of Teacher Education (IPG) graduates this year, appointing reserve candidates for critical options and recruiting teachers on a Contract of Service (COS) basis.
“A total of 3,150 people have already been appointed and are ready for placement in schools according to future needs,” he said.
On the haze issue, Wong said the MOE has clear guidelines on school activities based on the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading.
He said all outdoor activities would be suspended if the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed and online learning implemented if it exceeds 200.
“However, the MOE also takes into account parents’ concerns about their children’s health. If parents are still worried, they can choose not to send their children to school. That is the parents’ choice,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Blocked trails delayed six hikers’ return from Gunung Gerah, says Perak Fire Dept
Article:
GERIK, 8 Sept — The closure and obstruction of hiking trails that have not been used for a long time were the main reasons why the six hikers took a longer time to make their way before they were found safe last night, after participating in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, on August 29.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the hikers found that the trails at Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat were closed due to these factors.
“When they reached Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat, the found that the trails to both these hills were closed as they had not been used by hikers for a long time.
“Due to the difficulties faced, such as fallen trees, it resulted in them taking a longer time (to make their way out),” she said when met at Jeti Trojan, Tasik Banding, here today.
She said the hiking area’s lack of communication coverage also contributed to the loss of contact, thereby sparking concerns among the victims’ families before a police report was lodged.
The victims, she said, managed to reach Bukit Bongok and obtained a mobile phone signal to contact their families, enabling their exact location to be determined and for them to be safely rescued.
Earlier, the six hikers safely made their way out of Pos Kemar at 10.20am today via Jeti Trojan here.
The six — Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39; his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39; their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9; as well mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43 — were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic.
Previously, the six were reported missing after they went hiking at the mountain on August 29 and failed to exit the forest by the scheduled date, which was September 3, and family members lodged a police report on Sunday (September 6). — Bernama

Title: AirAsia resumes most flights disrupted by Anak Krakatau eruption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — AirAsia has resumed flights to and from destinations affected by the Anak Krakatau volcanic eruption following the reopening of Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
The airline said the airport had been temporarily closed since September 6 due to volcanic ash clouds from the eruption which posed a significant threat to safe aircraft operations in the vicinity of volcanic clouds.
“With Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport now reopened following its temporary closure since September 6, 2026, AirAsia has resumed affected services to and from Jakarta, with the exception of two flights on September 8, 2026,” it said in a statement today.
The two affected flights are QZ178 from Jakarta (CGK) to Bandar Lampung (TKG) and QZ179 from Bandar Lampung to Jakarta.
AirAsia said all affected guests had been notified of their flight status and recovery options, adding that it is working to ensure passengers could resume their journeys safely on the next available flight.
It advised guests travelling to or from the affected destinations to check their latest flight status on its website at airasia.com/flightstatus, as the weather situation remains fluid. — Bernama

Title: Perak Fire Dept calls for age limits on children joining high-risk mountain expeditions
Article:
GERIK, Sept 8 — The Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) recommends that the authorities review the standard operating procedure (SOP) regarding the age limit for children participating in extreme activities and hiking expeditions along challenging routes in mountainous areas.
Perak JPBM director Datuk Sayani Saidon (she) said the measure should be given attention to reduce risks when conducting such high-risk activities.
“This recommendation is because the risk of physical injury for children who go through challenging tracks is higher than adult climbers.
“If there is no standard (SOP), I feel it is time for the relevant department to look at this matter more carefully and transparently so that we can limit the involvement of climbers, especially underage ones, for the safety factor itself,” she said when met at the Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding, here, today.
Previously, six climbers who participated in the Trans Gerah Expedition in Gunung Gerah, Kelantan who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing while climbing the mountain on August 29, were safely released from Pos Kemar, 10.20 this morning.
The six victims involved, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Post Health Clinic Kemar.
Previously, the six victims were reported missing after climbing the mountain on August 29, after reportedly failing to leave the forest on the scheduled date, which was September 3, and family members filed a police report on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Police to record statements from six Gunung Gerah hikers after rescue
Article:
BAGAN SERAI, Sept 8 — Police will record statements from six hikers in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing during the hiking trip.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the six hikers would be taken to the Gerik District Police Headquarters (IPD) for documentation after being brought out from Pos Kemar.
“They will all be allowed to return home after the documentation process is completed. They are also reported to be in good health,” he said at a press conference at the Kerian IPD here today.
Asked whether the couple had committed an offence by bringing their two children on the hiking trip, Mohd Alwi said all four had valid permits.
“There was no issue (with the couple bringing their children along) as the permit included details of their family members,” he said.
Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, and their two children, Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, together with mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before being taken to the Pos Kemar Health Clinic for medical examinations.
The search and rescue (SAR) team and the victims left Pos Kemar at 8.30am today and arrived at Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding, at 10.20am before proceeding to the Gerik IPD.
The six began their hike on August 29 and were due to emerge from the forest on September 3.
A report was lodged by their family members on Sunday after they failed to return as scheduled. — Bernama

Title: Six Gunung Gerah hikers safely out of forest after days missing
Article:
IPOH, Sept 8 — Six climbers who participated in the Trans Gerah Expedition in Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing while climbing the mountain on August 29, have safely left Pos Kemar this morning.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, left Pos Kemar at 8.30 this morning and arrived at Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding at 10.20am.
“All the victims and the SAR (search and rescue) team arrived safely at Pos Kemar at approximately 9.15pm last night. All the victims underwent a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic and rested at the facility.
“They were then taken to the Gerik IPD by police for documentation and further action,” he said in a statement here.
Previously, the six victims involved were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic.
Earlier, the six victims were reported missing after climbing the mountain on August 29, after reportedly failing to leave the forest on the scheduled date, which was September 3, and family members filed a police report on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia plans 9GW of gas-fired power capacity by 2032 as demand rises, says economy minister
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — Malaysia expects about nine gigawatts (GW) of gas-fired power capacity to be deployed by 2032 as the country manages growing electricity demand while progressively phasing out coal-fired generation.
Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the capacity would form part of the country’s efforts to manage electricity demand, with the last coal-fired power plant expected to be retired in 2044.
Akmal Nasrullah said energy demand was showing an upward trend, driven by factors including population growth and higher consumption from energy-intensive sectors such as data centres.
“In terms of the projection for energy demand, definitely we see a pattern of increase. One is population growth.
“But number two, there is also an increase in energy consumption by high-usage sectors such as data centres,” he told reporters after the Energy Regulatory Insights 2026 here today.
He said weather and climate conditions could also change energy demand patterns, particularly as hotter conditions increase the need for cooling systems and air conditioning.
Against this backdrop, Akmal Nasrullah said managing energy demand would become as crucial as managing energy supply over the next five to 10 years.
“I think for the next five to 10 years, Malaysia must really remain disciplined enough to ensure our system is continuously upgraded, not just in terms of the power produced, but also the grid and infrastructure, so that our system remains affordable, safe and sustainable,” he added.
He said energy planning should not only focus on the megawatts that need to be deployed in the system, but also on energy efficiency and conservation.
Akmal Nasrullah said the planning would need to be managed by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation and the Energy Commission to ensure the country could manage demand while remaining committed to sustainability efforts and reducing the energy sector’s carbon footprint.
Earlier in his keynote address, Akmal Nasrullah outlined three priorities for the next phase of energy reform, starting with the need for a competitive and progressive energy market with clear and predictable rules and transparent access arrangements.
Secondly, he said expanding generation capacity must be supported by a modern grid that is intelligent, visible, secure and flexible, with grid modernisation under the 13th Malaysia Plan regarded as essential economic infrastructure to enable investments to connect faster, improve system efficiency and support reliable economic growth.
Thirdly, Akmal Nasrullah said energy efficiency must be treated as an energy resource in its own right, as it could reduce operating costs, ease pressure on the system and strengthen competitiveness.
He said the first National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP) exceeded its original target, delivering cumulative electricity savings of 60,886 gigawatt-hours, equivalent to RM16.1 billion in savings, from 2016 to 2025.
Under NEEAP 2.0, Malaysia is targeting an 11.6 per cent reduction in energy demand against the business-as-usual scenario by 2035, which is expected to help lower energy costs, ease pressure on the system and support more productive and competitive economic activity. — Bernama

Title: Selangor on track to top RM100b investment mark this year, says Amirudin
Article:
SEPANG, Sept 8 — Selangor is confident that the value of investments recorded by the state this year will exceed RM100 billion based on the current positive momentum, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the state recorded about RM70 billion in investments up to mid-year, with the investment trend very encouraging.
“We set a target of RM80 billion, similar to the achievement in 2025, but by mid-2026, we had reached RM70 billion.
“Following this trend, we strongly believe we will be able to exceed the RM80 billion target. In fact, if the trend is very good, we are confident we can create a record of more than RM100 billion,” he said in a press conference after the delivery of vacant possession (VP) ceremony for the NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP) here today.
Amirudin said Selangor’s strong investment performance was also driven by the state government’s strategy of consistently carrying out investment missions abroad, including to France, Germany, Saudi Arabia and South Korea, showing that efforts to attract investment were being made extensively.
He said the development of new industrial areas, including NSIP in Sepang, as well as the development of a third port on Carey Island, is expected to continue to boost investment activities in Selangor.
“If the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) operates as scheduled at the end of this year and so on, I think this will all be exciting in several northern areas (and Selangor),” he said.
Regarding NSIP, Amirudin said more than 200 factories are expected to start operating after obtaining approvals, with most companies currently involved being local enterprises.
“This area is part of the Integrated Development Region in South Selangor (IDRISS), which was included in the First Selangor Plan (RS-1), as I mentioned.
“RS-1 is not just planning on paper, but the delivery (project) that we have made, and we feel very proud as it is not just a government project, but an initiative from a private company that also received assistance and support from the state government,” he said.
NSIP, which has received several recognitions, covers approximately 368.26 hectares of prime land with a total gross development value of RM10.2 billion.
As the inaugural development under the IDRISS masterplan, NSIP remains a major contributor to the development of South Selangor as a strategic industrial corridor for high-impact investments and is well positioned to accelerate socio-economic and industrial growth across the region. — Bernama

Title: Johor ready for cloud seeding as El Nino looms from October
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — Johor is prepared to conduct cloud seeding exercises if any of the state’s 17 dams experience low water levels in preparation for the El Nino phenomenon by next month, said Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
He said the current situation is under control as the state government monitors the water levels in dams on a daily basis.
“We are just preparing to face the super El Nino phenomenon which is expected from October to December.
“As a precautionary measure, we have also reached out to the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) for cloud seeding preparations.
“Johor may request formcloud seeding exercises done earlier before the drought period. At present, cloud seeding has been carried out in several states but not in Johor yet,” he told reporters after attending a taxi driver’s programme in conjunction with the Visit Johor Year 2026 at the Johor Tourism Information Centre (Jotic) here today.
Mohamad Fazli said Johor’s water levels in all dams are still at a stable level and some are also at a cautionary level.
“There are dam capacities that can last for up to six more months and only the dam in Gunung Pulai is in alert stage at the moment,” he said, adding that there is a possibility that the dam in Macap will also be affected.
However, Mohamad Fazli said the state government has not finalised the dams to focus on for cloud seeding.
He said that apart from cloud seeding, several other initiatives will be carried out such as pumping water from one water source to another on a smaller scale.

Title: Azalina: Politicians could face corruption charges without political financing law
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Politicians could easily find themselves facing corruption cases if there is no political financing law in Malaysia to regulate financial aid given to them, Pengerang MP Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today.
Azalina, who is also Umno information chief and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), however made it clear that she was saying this in her personal capacity as an MP and lawyer.
“I, personally think as a lawyer, if there is no Political Financing Act, many politicians will be charged with corruption — easy, simple. People giving aid are considered as corruption because the intention is not explained, receipts are not given, not informed how much aid is to be given.
“That’s why if there is no Act for political financing, I see that there will be many more problems in this country. This is my personal opinion, not as Umno information chief. This is my personal opinion as Pengerang MP,” she said during her speech at a convention here.
Azalina was giving a speech to officiate the Political Financing Convention 2026, which was organised by the PM’s Department’s legal affairs division (BHEUU) together with think-tank Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (IDEAS) and the International Islamic University Malaysia.
In her speech as minister, Azalina acknowledged the reality that money is required for politics.
She said the real question would be where these funds come from, how it is received and used, and how far this process is transparent and accountable.
“Without a clear framework, political financing can open the way to conflict of interest, abuse of power, political corruption and undue influence in the decision-making process,” she said.
She added that there is a need to find a balance between transparency and accountability with the need to ensure that there continues to be democratic space and legitimate political participation.
In her speech, Azalina said the current government believes that the era of “government knows best and government knows all” is over, and that it is important to involve the public and stakeholders when drafing a new law.
She spoke of the importance of consulting political parties, as they will be the stakeholders and “users” of the proposed political financing law.
Later during a press conference, Azalina proposed that the BHEUU obtain written confirmation by every single registered political party in Malaysia about their stand on having a political funding law.
Azalina said the political parties could provide their written decision through their secretary-generals on their supreme council’s or highest leadership’s decision.
She added that she could then state how many political parties agree or disagree to having a political financing law when she presents the proposed law to the Cabinet.
“I’m suggesting to BHEUU to get an official response of all the political parties in our country.
“So I’m suggesting as a minister, please get an official reply from political parties because I also want to know which political party agrees and disagrees. Or maybe they have better suggestion, I don’t know,” she said, adding that she would be very surprised if parties that talk about anti-corruption do not agree to such a law.

Title: No data centre approval without enough water, power, says Selangor MB
Article:
SEPANG, Sept 8 — The Selangor government is closely monitoring water and power supply capacity amid the rapid expansion of data centres in the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the state would not approve data centre projects without ensuring adequate water and electricity supply, amid growing public concerns over the industry’s resource requirements.
“We are very aware of the concerns of the public related to power and water supply, and we are monitoring closely.
“Without enough water, definitely the data centre cannot be approved in Selangor,” he told reporters after witnessing the handover of vacant possession for NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP) Phase 1 here today.
Amirudin was commenting on NCT Alliance Bhd’s recent announcement that it had signed a term sheet for the proposed sale of a 100-acre land parcel within NSIP for a data centre development that could support up to 800 megawatts (MW) of capacity.
Amirudin said every data centre application must obtain approval from the Federal Data Centre Task Force, with power supply requirements to be cleared by Tenaga Nasional Bhd and water supply by Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd.
He said the state government is confident that its water supply capacity would be sufficient, particularly with the Rasau Water Supply Scheme expected to provide an additional 350 million litres per day (MLD), while the capacity could reach 700 MLD upon full completion of its first phase.
He also stressed that the state government is encouraging data centre operators to adopt water-recycling systems and technologies that could reduce water consumption for cooling purposes.
“We are encouraging the recycling of water … so that the processed water is not discharged, but instead recycled within each data centre,” he said.
Amirudin said the rapid expansion of data centres could also generate wider economic benefits by supporting the development of the electrical and electronics (E&E), chip and semiconductor sectors.
He added that Selangor had also introduced a 30 per cent policy to ensure small and medium enterprises (SMEs) benefited from data centre operations in the state. — Bernama

Title: Anwar urges younger generation to keep Tun Abdul Razak’s legacy, ideas alive in nation-building
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the younger generation not to merely remember the late Tun Abdul Razak Hussein as a historical figure, but instead to rekindle the torch of his struggle and ideas in confronting the challenges of nation-building.
Anwar said efforts to honour the contributions of the country’s second Prime Minister must be accompanied by a deep understanding of his ideas, thinking and values, so that these can serve as key guides in addressing current challenges.
He stressed that figures such as Tun Abdul Razak should not be viewed merely as part of the historical record, as his ideas and struggles continue to hold value and relevance for generations today and in the future.
“This figure was no ordinary person, and he did not come and go as a simple historical tale. That is why it is our responsibility to keep the flame of his struggle burning brighter.
“Remembering a statesman is no easy task. It can uncover history, inspire a longing for change, rekindle a sense of what is right to serve as lessons and guidance. Not to bury the ashes of the dead, but to rekindle its flame,” he said when delivering a speech at the Remembering Statesman Tun Abdul Razak: “Architect of Nation-Building” programme at the Tun Abdul Razak Memorial here today.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang.
The prime minister said Tun Abdul Razak’s ideas and spirit of struggle must continue to be kept alive because the vision he left behind remains relevant as a guide for present and future generations, rather than being regarded merely as part of history.
He said the late statesman played an important role as a wise helmsman in developing the country after independence, at a time when Malaysia was facing various challenges, including racial tensions, the communist threat and a weak economic position.
“Statesmen like Tun Abdul Razak were very wise and astute helmsmen. He sought out and assessed individuals, placing his trust in figures from the public and private sectors and bringing out the best in them with integrity to help him,” he said.
Anwar also shared his personal experience as a university student who had interacted with Tun Abdul Razak at his official residence, Seri Taman, where the latter took seriously and assessed the views and concerns of young people at the time.
He said the experience showed Tun Abdul Razak’s openness to listening to the views of young people who took a firm stance and called for change, even though their views might have been somewhat hard-hitting.
The prime minister said the New Economic Policy (NEP) was among the most important legacies of Tun Abdul Razak that must be understood based on its original objectives of restructuring the economy and eradicating poverty regardless of race.
He said the NEP should not be misconstrued as a policy that benefited only the elite or cronies, but was instead intended to uplift the dignity of the poor and provide opportunities for those with the ability to compete in entrepreneurship.
“I still remember our speeches and discussions at the time at Seri Taman. He said, the poor do not recognise skin colour... and coincidentally (at that time) the majority were Malays.
“For me, the NEP remains a very noble vision in terms of restructuring society and eradicating poverty regardless of race. Unfortunately, in the current narrative, it tends to be interpreted from a different perspective,” he said.
He said the government today had never wavered from its commitment to eradicating poverty comprehensively, thereby continuing the original spirit championed by Tun Abdul Razak.
The prime minister said the late statesman’s principles of restructuring society and eradicating poverty regardless of race remain relevant and need to be strengthened in line with current demands.
He also said the present generation should take heed of the second Prime Minister’s message on the country’s three main threats, or the “3Cs” — Communism, Communalism and Corruption.
He said although the armed communist threat no longer exists as it did in the past, the country must remain vigilant against the influence of foreign ideologies, while also addressing racial sentiments and corruption, which remain major challenges.
“Communalism remains deeply entrenched, while corruption continues to be one of the problems here,” he said.
Anwar said Tun Abdul Razak’s warning on corruption was highly significant, particularly his message to young people that integrity is easy to pledge before one assumes power, but the principle often wavers once a person gains a position of authority.
In this regard, he hoped the programme commemorating the statesman would not merely revisit the life and contributions of Tun Abdul Razak, but also highlight his ideas and thinking for the new generation to appreciate.
The Remembering Statesman programme was organised by the Ministry of National Unity through the National Archives and the Tun Razak Foundation, as part of efforts to commemorate and highlight the legacy of the country’s statesmen so that it continues to be known and appreciated by present and future generations. — Bernama

Title: Contractor fined RM20,000 after pleading guilty to using fake documents for RM5m Felda project
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — A 50-year-old contractor was fined RM20,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of using false documents to obtain a road resurfacing and drainage upgrade project under a Felda scheme worth RM5 million about three years ago.
Wan Shahrinizam Wan Ibrahim pleaded guilty to the two charges after they were read to him through an interpreter before Judge N. Kanageswari.
Kanageswari imposed a fine of RM20,000 for the two charges and ordered the accused to serve three months in prison for each charge if he failed to pay the fine.
The accused paid the fine.
According to the first charge, Wan Shahrinizam dishonestly used a document he knew to be false as genuine, namely bank account statements for November 2022 to January 2023 belonging to a company, which he instructed an officer to submit through the Felda e-Procurement System.
The documents were submitted as part of an application for a RM5 million project to resurface a village road and upgrade the drainage system at Felda Ciku 3, Gua Musang, Kelantan.
For the second charge, the accused dishonestly submitted documents he knew to be fake as genuine, namely a Letter of Acceptance of Tender for resurfacing works with premix and repairs to the drainage system at Jalan Parit Yaani and Parit Botak, Batu Pahat, as well as related works.
He had instructed the same officer to submit the documents through the same system for the same application.
A Letter of Acceptance of Tender is a formal written notice sent by a project owner or client to a contractor confirming that their bid or tender has been successful and creating a legally binding contract.
Wan Shahrinizam was charged with committing the offences at premises in Jalan Watan, Taman Desa 3, Parit Setongkat, Muar, in February 2023.
He was charged under Section 471 of the Penal Code (Act 574) for fraudulently or dishonestly using a forged document as genuine, an offence punishable under Section 465 of the same Code.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of two years, or a fine, or both upon conviction.
However, the court accepted the representation as a Take Into Consideration (TIC) against another related charge submitted by lawyers Azalea Nazihah and Muhammad Denial under Section 171A of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC).
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Irna Julieza Maaras appeared for the prosecution.

Title: Sungai Perak blue water caused by rain, minerals and changes in water flow, state assembly told
Article:
IPOH, Sept 8 — The phenomenon of Sungai Perak turning blue was caused by the interaction of several factors, including increased runoff following heavy rain, the presence of mineral particles and changes in water flow conditions, the Perak State Legislative Assembly was told today.
Perak Science, Environment and Green Technology Exco Teh Kok Lim said the finding was based on the Final Report of the Investigative Sampling (IS) Study on Sungai Rui, Gerik, conducted by experts from Scieno TW, a concessionaire appointed by the Department of Environment Malaysia.
He said the report was presented to the Perak State Executive Council on Aug 19.
“Based on the study and analysis, the experts concluded that the phenomenon was caused by the interaction of several factors, particularly increased runoff following heavy rain, the presence of mineral particles and changes in water flow conditions,” he said.
Teh was replying in writing to Kenering assemblyman Mohamad Husairi Arifin, who asked what caused the water in Sungai Perak near the Air Ganda Bridge in Hulu Perak to turn blue in early July, as well as the findings of the investigation and measures taken.
Teh said Hulu Perak was naturally rich in minerals, while heavy rainfall increased runoff, carrying more mineral particles from catchment areas, particularly open areas, into the river system.
He said data obtained by environmental scientist Dr Abd Rani Abdullah showed that rainfall during the phenomenon was almost twice as high as in the preceding period.
“This increased the volume of runoff and carried more mineral particles into the river system. However, rainfall and the presence of minerals alone were not sufficient to produce the colour-changing phenomenon.
“A certain concentration of minerals and suitable water flow conditions had to occur simultaneously,” he said.
Teh said Sungai Rui, being narrower, had a faster current, but the flow slowed when it entered the wider Sungai Perak.
“This allows fine mineral particles to remain suspended and accumulate for a longer period. When these particles interact with light, the scattering and reflection of light causes the water to appear bluish,” he said.
He said the types of minerals present, including copper, iron, aluminium and silica, as well as particle size, also influenced the optical properties and visible colour of the water.
On water quality, Teh said Sungai Perak was currently classified as Class II under the National Water Quality Index (WQI), based on an analysis of more than 30 water quality parameters.
He said the classification meant the river was suitable for uses prescribed under Class II, including recreational activities, fisheries and as a raw water source for conventional treatment before use.
Teh said the state government, through the Department of Environment (DOE), continuously carried out enforcement and inspections on premises subject to the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and its latest amendments.
“This included activities subject to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) requirements and industrial premises governed by the Environmental Quality (Industrial Effluent) Regulations 2009,” he said.
He said the DOE had eight manual monitoring stations and one automated monitoring station along the Sungai Perak Basin.
“Monitoring is carried out by the appointed concessionaire, while river water quality data is monitored online through the Environmental Quality Monitoring Programme.
“Manual monitoring is conducted six times a year,” he said.
Teh said any detected changes or deterioration in water quality would be notified to the DOE through the Notification of Pollution Event Level 1 or Level 2 (NPE 1/NPE 2) mechanism.
He said the early notification would allow the department to promptly identify potential pollution sources and take follow-up action.
On the way forward, Teh said the state government was considering legal, scientific and social aspects, as well as proposals from experts and residents in Hulu Perak.
Among the proposals was a Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) study to determine the pollution load received by Sungai Rui and Sungai Perak and to map or inventory pollution sources.
The state government also proposed establishing a state-level task force led by the Perak Water Resources Management Board to identify and coordinate action among agencies and strengthen collective enforcement.
Other proposals included studying the use of the Mine Rehabilitation Fund to rehabilitate former mining areas.
Teh said the government also planned to identify locations for installing online monitoring systems to obtain real-time data.
“Parameters including pH, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, total suspended solids and conductivity would be monitored as early indicators of abnormalities linked to mining activities,” he said.
He said the state government also planned to establish a Perak-level guideline for mining activities based on benchmarks and best mining practices adopted by leading mining countries.
“Based on these best practices, the state government can direct mining operations to be upgraded from time to time in line with the latest technology,” he said.

Title: Anwar says Cabinet consensus provides stability for govt to plan, implement policies
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Cooperation and consensus among members of the Cabinet are, as a whole, at a good level, thereby contributing to the country’s political stability, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this had enabled the government to plan and implement the country’s development agenda based on clear policies and a stable political environment.
“True, we cannot deny that our performance has been commendable because we have clear policies, political stability and cooperation within the Cabinet, although sometimes on social media it is a little different.
“But in terms of cooperation, we generally have good consensus and this provides an indication of stability and allows us to plan for the country,” he said when delivering his address during his meeting with the staff of the Ministry of Plantations and Commodities here today.
Anwar said the existing stability must be leveraged by the government to continue planning and implementing policies that benefit the country and the people as a whole.
At the same time, the Prime Minister reminded all parties not to become complacent with the achievements attained, but instead to continue striving to improve the government’s performance.
He said commendable achievements should not cause the government to “become complacent and bask in the comfort of success”, but should instead serve as an encouragement to continue working hard for the national interest.
“It’s true, it cannot be denied, our performance is commendable because of our clear policies, our political stability and the cooperation within the ministries, although sometimes on social media things are a little different,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said that economic growth in the second quarter of this year also recorded a better performance than expected despite facing challenges.
Malaysia is reported to have continued to record stronger-than-expected performance for three consecutive quarters, growing by six per cent in the second quarter of 2026 compared with 5.4 per cent recorded in the previous quarter.
This was the strongest second-quarter performance outside the pandemic period since 2014.
The second quarter 2026 performance brought the country’s first-half 2026 growth to 5.7 per cent, thus placing the Malaysian economy on a solid footing to achieve the government’s projected growth of between 4.0 per cent and 5.0 per cent for 2026. — Bernama

Title: Zambry: Malay, Bumiputera education must move beyond quotas towards self-reliance, resilience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The future of education for the Malay and Bumiputera communities must move beyond quotas towards greater self-reliance and resilience.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the success of the communities should instead be measured by their ability to excel in critical fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), develop new technologies and own intellectual property.
“The measure is not only the number of students entering university, but how many can think critically, master STEM, build global companies and lead world-class institutions,” he said when officiating the Malay Education Convention 2026 here today.
Zambry said that to achieve this goal, the country’s education ecosystem needed to move beyond simply providing access towards improving quality, building competencies, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing from technology use to technology ownership.
He said Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) should no longer be viewed as a second choice, but as a key pathway for developing national talent and producing highly skilled technicians and problem-solving experts.
Addressing the narrative of Bumiputera dependency, Zambry said affirmative policies remained relevant as long as structural imbalances persisted, but their ultimate objective must be to empower the Bumiputera community to achieve excellence and become independent.
“Malay and Bumiputera education cannot forever be built on the narrative that ‘we need to be helped because we are weak’.
“The narrative of the future must be: ‘We are given the opportunity to become strong, stand on our own, lead and help others’,” he said.
Zambry also stressed that mastery of the Malay language was important as a language of knowledge and identity, while proficiency in English and other languages was essential to competing globally without compromising integrity.
“In the pursuit of global excellence, we must never lose our identity and values. Education must produce not only intelligent people, but individuals of good character, integrity and the moral courage to lead,” he said.
On the convention, which is a continuation of the Bumiputera Education Congress held on May 1, Zambry said it would culminate in the formulation of a comprehensive resolution.
He said the resolution would subsequently be submitted to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi for consideration and further policy action by the government. — Bernama

Title: King receives 2026 Auditor-General’s Reports on federal, state finances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today received and reviewed the 2026 Auditor-General’s Reports on the federal and state governments’ financial management and activities.
The reports were presented to the King by Auditor-General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi during an audience at Istana Bukit Tunku here today.
Sultan Ibrahim was presented with the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 on the Federal Government Financial Statements for 2025.
He was also presented with the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2026 on the activities of federal ministries and departments, as well as reports covering the financial statements of state governments and agencies, activities of state ministries, departments and agencies, and the management of state government companies.
The King subsequently reviewed the reports in keeping with his concern over governance and the management of the country’s finances.
The details were shared by Sultan Ibrahim through his official Facebook page today.

Title: Rapid KL says passenger surge behind LRT congestion at Pasar Seni, Kajang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Increased passenger numbers caused congestion at the Kelana Jaya Line interchange at Pasar Seni and the Kajang Line this morning, Rapid KL said.
Rapid KL said no schedule delays were reported, while passenger flow and entry controls were being implemented at the affected stations to ensure safety and smooth movement.
“Please be informed that these interchange stations are experiencing an increase in passenger numbers, resulting in congestion.
“As such, to ensure passenger safety and the smooth movement of passengers, entry and passenger flow controls are being implemented at the affected stations,” Rapid KL said in a post on its social media accounts today.
Earlier, a video shared on social media by a Threads user known as nibukanyon showed crowded conditions at the stations.
The user also urged members of the public to postpone their journeys due to the congestion.
The video also claimed that LRT services had been experiencing a breakdown since yesterday and that the issue had yet to be repaired, while alleging that the stations were packed with passengers.

Title: Anwar: Asean haze mechanism needs stronger action, Malaysia won’t shield firms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said there was room to improve the existing Asean mechanism for tackling transboundary haze.
He stressed that the issue required more serious attention given its impact on public health.
“There is room for improvement.
“I think the Asean ministers must seriously look at it because this is affecting lives, particularly children and babies,” he told reporters when met at the Plantation and Commodities Ministry monthly assembly here today.
Anwar was responding to questions on whether the current Asean mechanism on transboundary haze was sufficient and whether stronger enforcement was needed.
He said the recurring impact of haze on neighbouring countries showed the need to assess whether existing regional mechanisms were sufficiently effective.
“The Asean ministers have to seriously look at this,” he said.
When asked on action taken against alleged perpetrators, Anwar said those were merely allegations as fires detected were mainly forest fires.
“Most of the fires that we detected were forest fires,” he said.
Anwar acknowledged that Malaysia had companies operating in Indonesia and would allow Indonesian authorities to take action if Malaysian firms were found to be involved.
“If there are Malaysian companies involved, we give room for Indonesia to take action.
“We certainly will not defend them,” he said.
Anwar’s remarks come as the region continues to grapple with the recurring problem of transboundary haze, which can affect air quality and public health across national borders.
